newsitem.title: USA: Phillips raises engineering plastics output.
newsitem.headline: Phillips raises engineering plastics output.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said Tuesday it is expanding its Ryton PPS (polyphenylene sulfide) facility in Borger, Texas, to 21.6 million pounds a year from 15.4 million pounds a yea.
The 40-percent increase will enable Phillips to supply growing market demand worldwide for Ryton PPS, according to Werner Lehnert, manager of engineering plastics for Phillips.
Construction in Borger is under way and will be completed by year-end 1997, Phillips said, adding the cost of the project was not disclosed.

Ryton PPS is an engineering plastic known for its heat and chemical resistance, as well as its ability to be molded to tight tolerances. Its uses include electronic components, under-the-hood automotive parts, appliances and fibers.
Phillips said it is the world's leading producer and seller of PPS.
The company noted it was the first commercial producer of PPS in the United States, with production beginning in Borger in 1972. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
